pr_title: view: send scale notification when the output is known
pr_body:
One of the nice things about explicit scale notifications is that it erases any confusion that would necessitate hacks like #6479. We should really take advantage of this to be nicer to fast clients, letting them know the intended scale as early as possible.

Ideally we would also send a better guess at the correct dimensions too, but that's a longstanding bug (can't find an issue for it though?) and a bit more of a hassle.

In practice, I observe the following less-than-ideal behavior on master: with the release of foot 1.15.2, my zsh prompt is reflowed after the first frame because the terminal initially has a larger number of columns than the 1.5 scale actually permits in the final window geometry. As a result, my zsh prompt begins on the second line instead of the first of a new terminal.
pr_comments: Ugh, this will change behaviour from scene and the scene branch would just regress this again. I'm not sure how scene should handle early scale values. Maybe we carry through this hack into the scene patches and iterate the whole surface tree to send the early scale. Which reminds me this MR doesn't handle subsurfaces, does that matter?

What's the interaction with scene? On the scene branch right now I observe that the preferred scale is sent correctly, just too late.

> Which reminds me this MR doesn't handle subsurfaces, does that matter?

I guess we should probably inform the subsurfaces too, and probably just send them all the same value as the toplevel surface.

I just ran into unexpected behavior in a software project of mine that is affected by what this appears to be trying to fix. I assume this is on hold because of the work being mentioned above hasn't been finished and/or merged yet?

I'm currently working around this, so this is by no means any sort of nudge to hurry this up, just interest in the project

Ref #8139 which does the same for layer-shell surfaces.

@rpigott, do you think you'd have time to update this PR?
I just rebased it for the conflict. Seems to work, but I'm not sure what the interaction with scene graph is.
We could have also added preferred buffer transform here as well
